newsitem.title: UK: Murdoch relative to launch new British tabloid.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch relative to launch new British tabloid.

text.p: A tabloid newspaper catering to Britain's ethnic minorities will be published on Monday, November 18, the publisher said on Friday.
The 64-page "New Nation" tabloid is the brainchild of Elkin Pianim, a Ghananian by birth,and a son-in-law of the media tycoon Rupert Murdoch.
Murdoch, who controls several major newspapers including the Times and the Sun, Britain's top-selling daily tabloid, has no connection to the publication, Kofi said.
"Rupert Murdoch has no financial, no editorial -- no connection whatsover to this newspaper," New Nation publisher Tetteh Kofi told Reuters in an interview.
He added that Murdoch's son-in-law had only a "financial interest" in the paper and would leave editorial decisions to the publisher and editorial staff.
The paper will provide news about black Britain and carry sections on sport, arts, fashion, beauty, lifestyle and women's issues, according to Kofi.
"We will be investigative and print stories that not only have legs but also reflect what's going on in the black community in Britain," he said.
The Afro-Caribbean publishing sector currently included three weekly titles with a combined weekly circulation of 60,000. Kofi said the New Nation needs 30,000 subscribers to break even.
